ddsmt.published: Kremer, Niemetz, Preiner, *ddSMT 2.0: Better Delta Debugging for the SMT-LIBv2 Language and Friends*, CAV 2021. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-81688-9_11
ddsmt.what: a delta debugger for SMT-LIB benchmarks
ddsmt.why: comparison data: an established tool serving the same solver, so that our own activity in a stretch can be read against something

murxla.published: Niemetz, Preiner, Barrett, *Murxla: A Modular and Highly Extensible API Fuzzer for SMT Solvers*, CAV 2022. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-13188-2_5
murxla.what: a model-based API fuzzer for SMT solvers
murxla.why: comparison data, and the nearest outside analogue to our own fuzzer, which we describe as a deliberate baseline

carcara.published: Andreotti, Lachnitt, Barbosa, *Carcara: An Efficient Proof Checker and Elaborator for SMT Proofs in the Alethe Format*, TACAS 2023. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-30823-9_19
carcara.what: a proof checker and elaborator for Alethe
carcara.why: comparison data, and an independent answer to a question this ecosystem also asks: how a proof produced by a solver gets checked

lfsc.published: Stump, Oe, Reynolds, Hadarean, Tinelli, *SMT proof checking using a logical framework*, Formal Methods in System Design 2012. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10703-012-0163-3
lfsc.what: the LFSC proof checker. **Its authors report it is deprecated and no longer useful**, which is their statement and not our assessment
lfsc.short: LFSC proof checker; deprecated by its authors
lfsc.why: comparison data with a different shape: a tool whose own authors have declared it done. Activity numbers for it are expected to be low and that is not a finding about it

lean-smt.published: Mohamed, Mascarenhas, Khan, Barbosa, Reynolds, Qian, Tinelli, Barrett, *lean-smt: An SMT Tactic for Discharging Proof Goals in Lean*, CAV 2025. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-98682-6_11
lean-smt.what: tactics for discharging Lean goals into SMT solvers
lean-smt.why: comparison data, and the closest outside neighbour to logos: it joins Lean and SMT from the other direction

iogos.why: its docs/maintenance.md records the `associate` footing and says the obligation is self-imposed, kept off the front page because the calculus is not installed yet and a declaration would oversell the tree
iogos.what: an executable proof checker for CPC in Isabelle/HOL, with the soundness scaffolding a proof development about it starts from. Its own README warns it is a research scaffold, not for use, with no soundness proof

isarare.published: Lachnitt, Fleury, Aniva, Reynolds, Barbosa, Nötzli, Barrett, Tinelli, *IsaRare: Automatic Verification of SMT Rewrites in Isabelle/HOL*, TACAS 2024. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-57246-3_17
isarare.what: generates Isabelle lemmas from RARE rewrite rules
isarare.why: comparison data, and the nearest thing to `iogos`, a tool we have only named: it already does in Isabelle what we have written down and not built

_comment: Who is in the Eunoia ecosystem, and on what footing. Read by the status
implementation here and the commands in scripts/. Checkouts resolve
through scripts/repos.local, which is written by hand.
`what` is the full description. Optional `short` supplies a concise purpose
for eo_status_audit, aiming for 60 characters or fewer. The table uses `short`
before `what` and shortens longer text to 60 characters with an ellipsis.
This is a list somebody maintains, not one anything derives: a footing is a
decision rather than a fact about a tree. `status` is the whole of what this
file asserts --
member      declares membership in its README, the check passes, and it
shares the approach docs/vision.md argues for. The second half
is a judgement and is not checked -- see below
associate   it holds *itself* to the shared policy and carries no
front-page declaration, recording what it is held to on its
own docs/maintenance.md. It owes us nothing, and the footing
is theirs to record rather than ours to assert -- see `The
footings` and `The associate protocol` in docs/policy.md,
which is the authority on what the word means. What is still
undecided there is whether the bare maintenance heading or
the paragraph naming this ecosystem is the ask; until it is,
an entry we would like on this footing says
`proposed: associate` and its `status` stays what it is
today. `vetted` is when a person last read their marker and
`why` is what it said
candidate   the policy is addressed to it and it has not joined. It may
still carry `vetted` and `why`, which say we have read it and
what we read it as; those are what a proposed footing rests
on and they oblige the tool to nothing
foundation  the arrangement is downstream of it. We place no constraint on
it, we ask it for nothing, and we say what it is to us. The
entry is a fact about *our* arrangement and never a status
conferred on theirs -- see docs/policy.md
child       a child project inside another repository here. `parent`
names whose tree, `path` where in it, and `branch` the
branch of the parent its current work is on, where that is
not the default one. A child is never a checkout of its own,
and its own README introduction controls its listing with
**Eunoia listing:** advertised or unadvertised. An absent
declaration means advertised; IDs still resolve through the
parent. A name with no work behind it is a
different thing and is not here at all. Naming ideas belong
in proposals; docs/glossary.md registers names in use
outsider    a tool outside the ecosystem that we track, and never propose
for promotion. docs/laws.md LAW 9 governs it. *Tracking* is
analysing our own positioning against it -- a finding about
us, never an assessment of them -- and what is permitted
requires a public repository and a publication, unless the
owners volunteer the tool under LAW 9.4. Keep the facts apart:
`released`   the public repository
`published`  the publication citation
Both fields are required. On volunteered entries, use
`unknown` for an unestablished fact and `none` only for an
established absence. Without an owner offer, leave a project
out of the register until both requirements are established.
`volunteered`  an optional object recording the owner's
offer: `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `owner` and
`evidence` (the statement or its reference)
Each offer field is a nonempty string. The audit checks the
record's form; a person verifies the evidence. Neither release
nor publication is implied by an offer. These fields are
printed in no table.
An outsider that may be tracked under docs/laws.md LAW 9 may also carry
`dioktes` under the same conditions. LAW 10
defines: this ecosystem is *in dioktes* when it is actively searching for
defects in a tool outside it. The field reads "<date began> -- <what closes
it>" and is a declaration, not a
footing: it says what we are doing, and nothing about them. It is removed
when the investigation ends. A maintainer's stop request ends public
reporting and further contact; private investigation may continue under
LAW 10.3 while LAW 9 still permits it. Nothing here currently carries one.
These are not a ladder. A member trades compliance for a claim we make; an
associate trades nothing and makes its own. Neither is above the other, and
reading the list as a ranking is the mistake docs/policy.md is written to
prevent.
`proposed` is an intention and never a fact. scripts/eo_status_audit
--protocol reports where each proposed associate stands against each version
of the drafted protocol; it returns 0 always, because a tool cannot fail a
rule that has not been decided.
`status` now carries one mechanical fact and, for a member, one judgement.
Only the mechanical half is ever read by a program: eo_status_audit --check
--online decides *declares / does not declare* for a member and a candidate,
and *records the associate marker / does not* on an associate's own
docs/maintenance.md. Whether a
member shares the approach is a vision question, nobody has the authority to
settle it, and no check here may ever acquire an opinion about it.
What is not in this list, deliberately: everything these tools are built
*with* rather than built *around*. Lean and its toolchain, the C++ ethos is
compiled by, Python, the CI runner. Several are more load-bearing than half
the rows here and none of them is a footing -- the line is subject matter,
not how much we rely on it, and this file lists tools built around the
calculus plus the one project all of it is downstream of. What those
dependencies cost is a different question, and it belongs to the auditor
described in tools/ynoia/docs/requests.md rather than here.
A status is changed by a person. An audit may report that one looks
wrong; nothing edits this file on its own.
This file's history starts on 2026-09-15, when the governance handoff moved
it here. **The earlier record is in anoieu**: `git log --follow --
scripts/ecosystem/ecosystem.json` includes its deletion on 2026-09-15 and
follows the rename from tools/ecosystem.json back to 2026-08-31.
A first revision is a state and not a
transition, so reading this file alone reports every entry it was born with
on the day it moved -- reported by epikrisis, 2026-09-17.
Two further fields, neither of which is a status:
joined     the commit of the repository that **held the shared policy**
when a member joined: `anoieu <sha>` for a join before the
2026-09-15 governance handoff, `kanon <sha>` for one after it.
That is why the value names a repository and not only a
commit -- the policy has moved once and is expected to move
again, and a bare sha would stop identifying anything the
moment it did. It is the only coordinate we actually have:
there is no X.Y.Z version of the policy and nothing is
versioned against a stretch, so a commit is the honest answer
until somebody decides otherwise.
It is not a checker pin. A pin identifies the checker and not
the policy, the two live in different repositories, and
docs/policy.md says under `The checker and this page now live
in different repositories` that a checker pin alone does not
identify the policy. A member's pin is in its own workflow
file, which is where it is read from.
Absent where it could not be established: we did not record
joins at the time, and reconstructing one means reading
somebody else's history. Which footings changed during the
current term, and when, is docs/history.md.
genuine    a judgement, never a check: that the repository was
*constructed* according to these policies rather than made to
pass them afterwards. It is a fact about a history and not
about a tree, so the policy checker cannot decide it and
must never try -- a tree retrofitted into compliance and a
tree built compliant are identical from the tree alone. It is
settled by reading the history, which is what an auditor of
histories is for, and it is a person's to record.
No entry carries it. Nobody has assessed one, and writing it
down unassessed would be the overclaim the field exists to
make visible. Note also that anoieu cannot ever be genuine:
it wrote the policies, so it could not have been constructed
according to them. The property distinguishes what came after
from what came first, which is most of why it is worth having.

aisthesis.short: How this ecosystem relates to other state-of-the-art AI systems
aisthesis.what: three documents about the practice of building this ecosystem rather than about the calculus: how that practice relates to the state of the art, what that reading implies somebody should build, and where writing about the future stops being a plan

anoieu.short: Static analyzer, fuzzer, and policy checker
anoieu.what: the static analyzer, the fuzzer, and the policy checker; the policy is kept by kanon

cvc5.short: SMT solver and owner of CPC
cvc5.what: the solver, and the owner of CPC. The ecosystem exists to serve it, and asks it for nothing

ethos.short: C++ proof checker and Eunoia manual
ethos.what: the proof checker, the home of the Eunoia manual, and the tree the ethos-eoc child project is in
ethos.why: every other reading of the language is measured against its behaviour, and this repository's oracle is a recording of it

ethos-eoc.what: the Eunoia compiler, and the semantics sets it ships

logos.what: Lean-based proof checker, and the owner of Cpc.eos

eudaimonia.short: Calculus template: a signature, checker, and proofs
eudaimonia.what: the calculus template: bring a signature, get a checker and its proofs

dokimasia.short: Finds gaps in cvc5's proof production
dokimasia.what: reads cvc5's proof-production C++ and asks what no proof step covers

paideia.why: it houses two child projects this register already carried, so a parent it can be reached through has to exist here; its front page calls it an associate, but its docs/maintenance.md explicitly leaves the footing marker unrecorded
paideia.short: A developer's guide to cvc5's source
paideia.what: a written account of how cvc5's codebase is put together, for people who have to change it, and the tree anakrisis and empeiria moved into on 2026-09-18

tachyon.short: Searches for ways to improve cvc5 performance
tachyon.what: searches for ways to improve cvc5 performance, using reproducible benchmark experiments to test proposed changes

eschaton.short: Compares approaches to better-founded SMT solvers
eschaton.what: compares approaches to better-founded SMT solvers and their costs

epikrisis.what: audits how these repositories have changed over time, on evidence a reader can re-derive

kanon.what: the ecosystem's governance: the policy, vision, laws and inventory

koine.what: the (shared) tooling no other tool wants to maintain

sapheneia.what: Eunoia described as a language definition rather than as a checker's manual

ynoia.short: Questions the ecosystem's design and what it lacks
ynoia.what: whether the ecosystem's arrangement earns its machinery, and what it is missing

euthyna.short: Examines the structure and weight of Logos's proofs
euthyna.what: what the proof in logos is made of, and where its weight sits

martyria.short: Ethical concerns, responses, and evidence of conduct
martyria.what: specific ethical concerns, with a stance attached: what we do about one situation, and what can be shown about how we behaved in it

zetesis.short: Examines ethical standards and evidence of meeting them
zetesis.what: the general inquiry: what standard this ecosystem is held to, taken from outside, and whether our record could show we met it

stathmos.short: Audits ecosystem status and keeps the report card
stathmos.what: audits the ecosystem register against repository declarations and local policy checks; separately writes and keeps the report card against the vision, at recorded versions -- those grades are human judgements, never automated, and a person may overrule any of them

tekmerion.what: the evidence that what these documents say is still true, claim by claim -- why anybody should believe the prose this ecosystem mostly consists of

workflow-launcher.short: Guides a new tool's first hour and records lessons
workflow-launcher.what: the first hour of a new tool's life, and a register of what this ecosystem's practice has turned out to be doing

anakrisis.short: Reviews cvc5 PRs for changes in proof completeness
anakrisis.what: examines cvc5 pull requests by comparing dokimasia's proof-completeness analyses before and after a change, and records what its review adds

empeiria.short: Works cvc5 bug reports and learns from maintainer feedback
empeiria.what: works cvc5's public bug reports and records what the maintainers' responses teach about the next fix

telos.short: Researches a proof-first SMT solver checked by Logos
telos.what: research toward a proof-first SMT solver whose output is checked by Logos, using dokimasia's analyses to guide the design

apodeixis.short: Proposed Alethe stress test of Eudaimonia; paused
apodeixis.what: a proposed Alethe stress test of the Eudaimonia framework; work is paused pending collaboration and permission from the Alethe maintainers

noesis.what: research toward a verified Eunoia-to-Lean compiler, with explicit preservation claims for each pass

hermeneia.short: Connects embedded SMT-LIB semantics to Lean's logic
hermeneia.what: researches correspondence definitions and lemmas that carry checked refutations from embedded SMT-LIB semantics into native Lean propositions

mimesis.short: Teaches Eunoia signature writing from worked examples
mimesis.what: how a Eunoia signature is written and how one gets into Logos, in two strands: case studies of episodes that already happened, and tutorials that build a signature from a calculus's rule descriptions

cvc6.short: Proposes automated refactoring of cvc5; nothing built
cvc6.what: a research position proposing agent-driven maintenance and refactoring of cvc5, retaining its design; a working title, with no implementation

hawkeye.short: Intention to build a new solver with agents; one page
hawkeye.what: a one-page intention to build a new SMT solver from nothing, written mostly by autonomous agents; nothing is built

elaphros.short: Measures and reduces cvc5's proof-production overhead
elaphros.what: measures what producing a proof costs cvc5 in time and memory against solving the same problems without one, attributes the overhead, and tests optimizations against a pinned baseline

heuresis.short: Finds cvc5 performance issues, esp. for quantifiers
heuresis.what: investigates cvc5 performance shortcomings in quantified benchmarks where z3 is much faster, recording enough evidence for a human to judge which are worth pursuing

metagraphe.short: Finds missing cvc5 rewrites, esp. for strings and BV
metagraphe.what: finds concrete gaps in cvc5's rewriting and simplification for strings and bit-vectors, each with a small reproducible example and the evidence behind it
